title: Judge Advocate (I) (Col to 2ndLt) PMOS, SJA to CMC
raw_text:
1.     MOS 4402, Judge Advocate (I) (Col to 2ndLt) PMOS, SJA to CMC

    a. Summary. Judge Advocates provide legal support to commanders,
Marines, Sailors, and their families to promote readiness and to contribute
to mission accomplishment. Judge advocates provide legal support in the
following six functions: military justice, international and operational law,
administrative law, civil law, legal assistance, and legal administration.
As company grade officers, judge advocates ordinarily serve at law centers as
litigators or legal assistance attorneys, or in staff judge advocate offices
as command legal advisors. Litigation opportunities exist as special trial,
trial, defense, and victims legal counsel in courts-martial; as Special
Assistant United States Attorneys in United States Federal Court; and as
recorders, counsel for the respondent, or victims’ legal counsel in
administrative discharge boards. As majors, Judge Advocates may serve as
staff judge advocates or deputy staff judge advocates providing command legal
advice, or as litigators in the billets of special trial counsel, military
justice officer, senior defense counsel, or regional victims legal counsel.
Lieutenant Colonels may serve as staff judge advocates, deputy staff judge
advocates, regional special trial counsel, regional trial counsel, regional
defense counsel, or Law Center Directors. Colonels may serve at
Headquarters, Marine Corps, as staff judge advocates, or as the chief counsel
or senior leader in the Office of Special Trial Counsel, Trial Services
Organization, Defense Services Organization, or Victims Legal Counsel
Organization. All field grade judge advocates may serve as military judges
after being screened by a judicial screening board.

       b.    Prerequisites

             (1) The 4402 MOS is assigned as a primary MOS to an officer who has:

            (a) Obtained a juris doctor from a law school that at the time of
graduation was approved by the American Bar Association (ABA).

            (b) Been admitted to the practice of law before a federal court
or the highest court of a state, territory, commonwealth, or the District of
Columbia.

       c.    Requirements

             (1) Complete one of the following:

                 (a) Complete the Basic Lawyer Course (N0501P1).

            (b) Upon the written recommendation of the SJA to CMC, the Judge
Advocate General may, when in the best interests of the Marine Corps, waive
the requirement to complete the Basic Lawyer Course (N0501P1), certify the
officer under Article 27(b), UCMJ, and designate the officer as a judge
advocate.

        (2) Any 4402 assigned to a litigation billet must complete Military
Justice Orientation (N05Y221). This course may be completed immediately
following completion of the Basic Lawyer Course (N0501P1).

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks refer to
reference (bh), Legal Services Training and Readiness Manual.

 1127                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L



       e.   Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

            (1) Judges, Magistrate Judges, and Magistrates 23-1023.

            (2) Lawyers 23-1011.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
